approvals.summary: This SOP provides step-by-step instructions to install IBM Db2 Community Server Edition on a Linux server (Worker1OL) and set up a db2inst1 service account. The procedure ensures proper installation, permissions, and configuration of Db2 database services for the system.
proposedCommands: ssh root@192.168.56.10 "yum install -y libaio libgcc libstdc++"
ssh root@192.168.56.10 "su - db2inst1 -c 'db2 create database SAMPLE'"
approvals.kbTitle: SOP: Install IBM Db2 Community Server and Configure db2inst1 Service Account on Worker1OL

safetyChecks.check: Verify sufficient disk space: df -h /tmp /opt | awk '$NF ~ /%/ { if ($5+0 > 80) exit 1}'
Ensure no prior db2inst1 user exists: id -u db2inst1 2>/dev/null && echo 'User already exists, aborting' && exit 1 || echo 'User does not exist, proceeding'
Validate integrity of Db2 tarball: tar tzf /tmp/db2_v11.5.8_linuxx64_server.tar.gz >/dev/null || (echo 'Tarball is corrupted, aborting' && exit 1)
Confirm installation was successful: su - db2inst1 -c 'db2level' | grep 'DB2 v11.5' || (echo 'Db2 installation failed' && exit 1)
Verify database SAMPLE creation: su - db2inst1 -c 'db2 list database directory' | grep SAMPLE || (echo 'Database SAMPLE not created' && exit 1)

approvals.aiReasoning: The steps outlined install IBM Db2 Community Server using a standard install script provided by IBM in the tarball, which ensures compatibility and correct setup. Prerequisite libraries are installed to support Db2 operations. The db2inst1 service account is a requirement for running Db2 instances and will have its .ssh folder correctly created with proper permissions. Safety checks ensure that the installation only proceeds if disk space, prerequisites, and user states allow for a successful setup.

ssh root@192.168.56.10 "yum install -y libaio libgcc libstdc++"
ssh root@192.168.56.10 "mkdir -p /opt/db2install"

ssh root@192.168.56.10 "echo 'export PATH=$DB2_HOME/bin:$PATH' >> /etc/profile.d/db2env.sh"
ssh root@192.168.56.10 "echo 'export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$DB2_HOME/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH' >> /etc/profile.d/db2env.sh"
ssh root@192.168.56.10 "source /etc/profile.d/db2env.sh"

This SOP covers systematic diagnosis of systemd-managed services (Grafana, custom dashboards), containerized dashboards (Podman/Docker/CRI-O), and Kubernetes static pods, including dependency checks (database, reverse proxy, TLS certs) and log analysis to restore service availability.
proposedCommands: ssh root@192.168.56.10 "systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running | grep -iE 'grafana|dashboard|prometheus|kibana|netdata|cockpit|nginx|traefik|haproxy' || echo 'No obvious dashboard services found in systemd'"

ssh root@192.168.56.10 "crictl ps -a 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'dashboard|grafana|kibana|console|prometheus|nginx|traefik' || docker ps -a 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'dashboard|grafana|kibana|console|prometheus|nginx|traefik' || podman ps -a 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'dashboard|grafana|kibana|console|prometheus|nginx|traefik' || echo 'No containerized dashboard found via crictl/docker/podman'"
ssh root@192.168.56.10 "ls -1 /etc/kubernetes/manifests/ 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'dashboard|grafana|console' || echo 'No static pod manifests for dashboard'"

ssh root@192.168.56.10 "systemctl status grafana-server 2>/dev/null || systemctl status grafana 2>/dev/null || systemctl status netdata 2>/dev/null || systemctl status cockpit 2>/dev/null || echo 'Checking for custom dashboard services...'"

ssh root@192.168.56.10 "journalctl -u grafana-server -n 100 --no-pager 2>/dev/null || journalctl -u grafana -n 100 --no-pager 2>/dev/null || journalctl -u netdata -n 100 --no-pager 2>/dev/null || journalctl -u cockpit -n 100 --no-pager 2>/dev/null || journalctl -xeu $(systemctl list-units --type=service --all | grep -i dashboard | awk '{print $1}' | head -1) -n 100 --no-pager 2>/dev/null || echo 'Checking container logs...'"

ssh root@192.168.56.10 "CONTAINER_ID=$(crictl ps -a 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'dashboard|grafana|kibana|console' | awk '{print $1}' | head -1) && [ -n "$CONTAINER_ID" ] && crictl logs --tail=100 $CONTAINER_ID 2>/dev/null || DOCKER_ID=$(docker ps -a 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'dashboard|grafana|kibana|console' | awk '{print $1}' | head -1) && [ -n "$DOCKER_ID" ] && docker logs --tail=100 $DOCKER_ID 2>/dev/null || PODMAN_ID=$(podman ps -a 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'dashboard|grafana|kibana|console' | awk '{print $1}' | head -1) && [ -n "$PODMAN_ID" ] && podman logs --tail=100 $PODMAN_ID 2>/dev/null || echo 'No container logs retrieved'"

ssh root@192.168.56.10 "systemctl is-active --quiet grafana-server && systemctl restart grafana-server || systemctl is-active --quiet grafana && systemctl restart grafana || systemctl is-active --quiet netdata && systemctl restart netdata || systemctl is-active --quiet cockpit && systemctl restart cockpit || echo 'No systemd dashboard service to restart'"

ssh root@192.168.56.10 "CONTAINER_ID=$(crictl ps -a 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'dashboard|grafana|kibana|console' | awk '{print $1}' | head -1) && [ -n "$CONTAINER_ID" ] && crictl stop -t 30 $CONTAINER_ID && crictl start $CONTAINER_ID || DOCKER_ID=$(docker ps -a 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'dashboard|grafana|kibana|console' | awk '{print $1}' | head -1) && [ -n "$DOCKER_ID" ] && docker restart $DOCKER_ID || PODMAN_ID=$(podman ps -a 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'dashboard|grafana|kibana|console' | awk '{print $1}' | head -1) && [ -n "$PODMAN_ID" ] && podman restart $PODMAN_ID || echo 'No container to restart'"

ssh root@192.168.56.10 "journalctl -u grafana-server -n 50 --no-pager 2>/dev/null | tail -20 || journalctl -u grafana -n 50 --no-pager 2>/dev/null | tail -20 || journalctl -u netdata -n 50 --no-pager 2>/dev/null | tail -20 || journalctl -u cockpit -n 50 --no-pager 2>/dev/null | tail -20 || echo 'Final log check complete'"
approvals.kbTitle: SOP: Troubleshoot Dashboard Service Unavailability on Worker Node

safetyChecks.check: Verify dashboard service is listening on expected port(s) post-restart
Confirm HTTP/HTTPS endpoint returns 2xx/3xx status code
Check disk space on /var/lib/<dashboard> and /var/log partitions > 15% free
Ensure no OOM kills in dmesg -T | grep -i kill
Validate dependent services (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, etcd) are running if dashboard uses them
Confirm SELinux/AppArmor not blocking dashboard ports (ausearch -m avc -ts recent)

approvals.aiReasoning: Worker nodes commonly host dashboards via systemd (Grafana, Netdata, Cockpit), containers (Kubernetes Dashboard, OpenShift Console, custom apps), or static pods. The SOP starts with service discovery across all three runtimes, checks resource constraints (disk/memory), retrieves relevant logs for root cause (OOM, config error, cert expiry, DB connectivity), performs targeted restarts, and validates via port listen and HTTP health checks. Commands are idempotent and safe for production use.

approvals.kbTitle: SOP: Troubleshoot Dashboard Service Unavailability on Linux Worker Node

safetyChecks.check: Verify target server IP (192.168.56.10) matches CMDB record for Worker1OL before executing SSH.
Confirm maintenance window approval or stakeholder acknowledgment before restarting production dashboard services.
Ensure backup of persistent data volumes (Grafana /var/lib/grafana, Prometheus /prometheus) exists prior to container recreation or filesystem repair.
Validate that the dashboard service is managed by systemd OR container runtime, not both simultaneously (double-management causes port conflicts).
Check firewall rules (firewalld/iptables/nftables) and SELinux/AppArmor audit logs if service binds locally but fails remote access.

approvals.aiReasoning: Dashboard unavailability on a generic Linux worker typically stems from: 1) Service crash (OOM kill, config error, dependency failure), 2) Container runtime issues (image pull failure, volume mount corruption, restart loop), 3) Resource exhaustion (disk full on /var/lib/docker or /var/lib/grafana, memory pressure), or 4) Network stack issues (port conflict, firewall drop). The steps prioritize non-intrusive discovery (ss, ps, systemctl, docker/crictl) before taking corrective actions (restart). Idempotent checks (systemctl is-active, docker ps -q) prevent errors if the service is managed differently than assumed. Verification uses local curl to isolate network path issues from application health.

approvals.incidentTitle: Memory utilization is 100 % on Worker1OL
approvals.summary: Worker1OL (192.168.56.10) reports 100% memory utilization, risking OOM kills and pod evictions. This SOP identifies the top memory consumers, checks for OOM events, safely clears reclaimable kernel caches, and restarts the highest-impact container runtime or service to restore headroom without reboot.
proposedCommands: ssh root@192.168.56.10 "dmesg -T | grep -i -e oom -e kill -e memory | tail -n 30"
ssh root@192.168.56.10 "crictl stats --no-trunc 2>/dev/null || docker stats --no-stream 2>/dev/null || echo 'Container runtime not found or no containers running'"
ssh root@192.168.56.10 "sync && echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches && echo 'Pagecache, dentries and inodes dropped'"
ssh root@192.168.56.10 "systemctl status kubelet containerd docker 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'Active:|Memory:' | head -n 10"
ssh root@192.168.56.10 "systemctl restart containerd 2>/dev/null || systemctl restart docker 2>/dev/null || echo 'No container runtime service to restart'"
ssh root@192.168.56.10 "sleep 10 && free -h && echo '---' && ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -n 10"
ssh root@192.168.56.10 "journalctl -u kubelet --since '30 min ago' --no-pager | grep -i -e memory -e oom -e evict | tail -n 20"

approvals.kbTitle: SOP: Create Read-Only Monitoring User on WorkerNode1HL

safetyChecks.check: Verify 'priya' exists in /etc/passwd with UID >= 1000 and shell /bin/bash
Confirm home directory /home/priya owned by priya:priya with 700 permissions
Validate password authentication works: su - priya -c 'whoami' (expects 'priya')
Ensure no sudoers entry exists for priya: ls -l /etc/sudoers.d/ | grep -v priya
Confirm account is not locked: passwd -S priya (expects 'P' or 'PS' status)

approvals.aiReasoning: The ticket requests a read-only monitoring account for NOC analyst Priya Nair. Following L2 user provisioning standards, we create the user idempotently with a descriptive comment field, set the provided password via chpasswd for automation safety, configure the .ssh directory for future key-based access hardening, and explicitly omit sudoers configuration to maintain least-privilege posture. Validation steps prove account existence, correct shell, password functionality, and absence of elevated privileges.

synthesizerOutput.synthesizedSolution:
ssh root@192.168.100.102 "id -u priya &>/dev/null || useradd -m -s /bin/bash -c 'Priya Nair' priya"
ssh root@192.168.100.102 "echo 'priya:Monitor@2026' | chpasswd"
ssh root@192.168.100.102 "mkdir -p /home/priya/.ssh && chmod 700 /home/priya/.ssh && chown -R priya:priya /home/priya/.ssh"
ssh root@192.168.100.102 "id priya && ls -ld /home/priya"
